A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RobSelf work, with matching equations, datasets and retained results. Text, equations, figures and tables are readable. Neither supplied PDF includes an appendix; both reference separate supplementary material that is not included and cannot be assessed.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthesized and real-world super-resolution experiments, component ablations and runtime measurements in Tables 1-5.

after.justification: v3 retains the original experiments and reports additional comparator results and qualitative alignment and robustness analyses.

M1.justification: The translator, deformable-convolution/resampling variants, content-aware filter and optimization objective remain substantively unchanged in Section 3 and Eqs. (1)-(6). Revised diagrams and explanations do not establish a changed algorithm.

E1.justification: The three principal tasks and collected data retain their coverage, group counts and resolutions despite removal of the RealMisSR name. v3 additionally uses EPFL RGB-NIR to train supervised comparators and explicitly evaluates well-aligned synthesized depth SR in Figure 12.

E2.justification: Table 3 adds Fusion-ArF, Fusion-CAP, PAN and HSI SR to the NIR comparison, previously restricted to self-supervised comparators. Figure 10 newly compares against MURF registration modules. Table 2 also extends the quantitative ×4 depth comparison to supervised methods previously left unscored. MOMNet is discussed but explicitly not evaluated.

E3.justification: For real-world ×4 depth SR, Table 2 replaces NIQE with depth-specific DSS and broadens the quantitative comparison beyond self-supervised methods. New NIR comparators are trained on EPFL RGB-NIR with synthesized misalignment. Section 5.1 changes the stated initial learning rate from 0.002 to 0.001; this documents a setting revision without establishing that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The component ablation in Table 4 is retained. New Section 5.6 substantially broadens analysis through comparison with registration modules under viewpoint variation and non-rigid motion (Figure 10), a missing-guide-structure case study (Figure 11), and a well-aligned-input comparison (Figure 12). These additions are qualitative.

E5.justification: Neither supplied version reports repeated-run counts, optimization seeds, confidence intervals, variability estimates or significance tests. Randomized misalignment generation concerns data construction rather than uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Table 2 replaces RobSelf-Re/De's ×4 depth NIQE scores of 11.24/11.25 with DSS scores of 8.4/8.6; these different metrics do not demonstrate a performance gain. Table 3 adds four comparators, with ×2 RMSE values of 6.58, 4.40, 5.19 and 4.52. Figures 10-12 add qualitative findings. Tables 1, 4 and 5 and the retained Table 3 scores remain numerically unchanged.

T1.justification: Eqs. (1)-(6) retain the same mathematical content, with notation and presentation adjustments. Neither version supplies formal propositions or proofs. DSS is introduced as a cited evaluation metric without a new mathematical definition or derivation.

C1.justification: The central self-supervision, performance and efficiency claims remain. v3 adds an explicit contribution claim about handling missing guide structures. It stops promoting RealMisSR as a named, standalone contribution in the abstract and conclusion, while retaining the collected data for evaluation.

C2.justification: v3 attributes recovery of missing guide structures to borrowing contextually related guide content under the translation objective. It also explains why the bare ablation baseline can outperform methods that excessively fuse misaligned guidance. The earlier discussion of NIQE favoring spurious depth textures disappears following the metric replacement; other main mechanism explanations remain.

D1.justification: v3 newly identifies Azure Kinect DK and describes randomized acquisition motions, documents training data for the added supervised baselines, and revises the learning rate. It omits v1's explicit prediction-head sharing annotation and separate-head statement for NIR. The principal hardware, iteration budget and underlying repository link remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 replaces much of the historical and dataset survey with direct positioning against MOMNet, SFG and misalignment-aware work in HSI SR, pan-sharpening, fusion, MRI and depth refinement. Added and removed citations accompany a substantive emphasis on joint translation versus conventional alignment, rather than merely bibliographic updates.

P1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, related work, dataset narrative and experimental prose are extensively rewritten. The dataset section is renamed, repeated Methods/Results paragraph labels are removed, and Interesting Observations becomes a separate subsection. These changes substantially reshape the narrative beyond renumbering.

P2.justification: The document switches from two-column to single-column formatting. Figures 2-4 are redrawn with different illustrative features, Figure 8 uses a different NIR example and adds Fusion-CAP, Figures 10-12 are added, and Table 3 gains comparator columns. Existing figures and tables are extensively repositioned and resized.

improvement.justification: The supervised NIR comparisons in Table 3 and targeted analyses in Figures 10-12 give the robustness claims broader support than v1 provides. DSS also adds a depth-specific assessment, although replacing NIQE does not establish better model performance. The gains are limited by qualitative-only boundary evidence, an unexplained learning-rate revision and omitted prediction-head details. Overall, the empirical support improves without a substantial change to the established method or retained results.
